newsitem.title: INDIA: Blast kills seven in Kashmir - news agencies.
newsitem.headline: Blast kills seven in Kashmir - news agencies.

text.p: Seven relatives of a campaign worker for Kashmir's ruling National Conference party were killed in a powerful blast on Monday, news agencies said.
They quoted officials as saying suspected Moslem militants triggered the blast at the residence of Ghulam Hassan Nadeef in the southern Kashmir district of Anantnag.

The attack came two days after Kashmir's newly elected Chief Minister Farooq Abdullah told separatist militants to surrender their arms within 30 days. There has has been no official response from the rebels.
The Press Trust of India and the United News of India, which reported the blast, gave no further details.
Abdullah's National Conference gained an absolute majority after last month's assembly elections in India's state of Jammu and Kashmir, the first polls there in nine years.

Hospital and police sources say at least 20,000 people have been killed in the separatist violence, which erupted in the Kashmir valley in 1990. Abdullah said recently the toll could be closer to 50,000.
